carmen: heads-up, nightly e2e perf spike on seqlen=128 for T4 pool after the kernel-autotune change (commit f9a2d3c). p99 tokens jumped ~2.4x.

raj: ugh. seen anything in profiler? flamegraph or kernel breakdown?

perf-bot: nightly-run: model=resnet-llm-7b, backend=nvptx, workload=streaming-chat, seqlen=128, batch=4, commit=f9a2d3c. p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=162ms (baseline p99=68ms).

mia: @carmen can you paste the profiler snippet? curious if it's a kernel-choice flip or kv-cache missstorm.

carmen: quick snapshot from nvprof: ````
GPU Kernel: attention_mixed_fp8_fastpath  time=90.3ms  calls=1
GPU Kernel: attention_generic_bf16       time=28.1ms  calls=1
GPU Kernel: kv_cache_apply_patch          time=12.4ms  calls=2
Total GPU time ~135ms
````
looks like we're picking attention_mixed_fp8_fastpath for seqlen=128 but that kernel is slower on SM7.5 T4s due to shared-mem layout mismatch. on sm8+ TC it was faster.

dylan: hm that matches my microbench. fp8 fastpath assumes tensor core warp-tile of 128x64 and fma-packing; on SM7.5 we emulate with lots of memcpy and alignment fixes -> regress.

raj: so autotuner picked fp8 path because commit broadened capability flags mapping: we started treating sm>=7 as "fp8-capable" instead of checking driver + hw feature bits. likely a false-positive.

olga: can we gate on a tighter probe: check PTX compute capability and cuda driver reports tensorCore fp8 support flag rather than SM alone? saves a misroute.

carmen: repro command I used: ````
./run_infer.sh --model resnet-llm-7b --device auto --batch 4 --seqlen 128 --commit f9a2d3c --profile nvprof > /tmp/prof.log
````
profile attached inline excerpt above.

perf-bot: quick diff vs baseline: kernel path changed at autotune step. Autotuner heuristic file had rule: `if sm_major >=7 then prefer fp8_fastpath` (old behavior used composite check).

mia: can we add a runtime capability probe that validates microbench latency for the selected kernel on boot and fall back if p99 > threshold? e.g. run a 50-step microbench with typical seqlen distribution.

dylan: agreed. propose: probe order -> check driver_feature_flags + run tiny microbench for candidate kernel (seqlen=64/128/256) -> commit selection. we already have microbench harness at tools/kernel_probe.sh.

olga: downside: extra probe time on first boot, but we can cache results per card serial and driver combo. obviously needed for Dedicated where card types vary.

raj: also KV cache interaction: when fastpath was used we saw double calls to kv_cache_apply_patch; might be because kernel layout expects packed KV but runtime produced unpacked format for sm7.5 -> extra conversion cost. need to assert KV layout invariant per kernel.

carmen: patch idea: revert broad capability mapping, add explicit hw-feature query `cudaGetDeviceAttribute(CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_AMD_FP8_SUPPORT?)` (pseudo) and probe microbench. plus a runtime assert that kernel->kv_layout==runtime_kv_layout or fall back.

perf-bot: Suggested guard: if microbench_p99(candidate) > 1.6 * microbench_p99(best_known) then disable candidate for this device. Also log telemetry: kernel_choice, device_serial, driver_version, microbench_latency.

infra-bot: rolling canary plan: 1) disable fp8_fastpath on all existing T4 pools by default, 2) land probe + caching, 3) re-enable fastpath for devices that pass. rollouts via config flag `hw_probe_fp8_validation=true`.

mia: can someone file a quick issue with repro steps and attach nvprof? i'll prioritize a small patch.

carmen: created issue #6312 with logs and steps. I'll try a local patch to force fallback and test.

dylan: one more note: add a tiny unit in autotuner to prefer kernels that minimize additional memcpy conversions for KV cache. we can compute a conversion_cost metric at probe time.

raj: ok sgtm. thanks team. :thumbsup: let's avoid broad sm-based heuristics going forward.

olga: fyi I'll add a telemetry field `kernel_probe_reason` to help debug future flips.

carmen: updated plan: revert change, land probe+microbench, cache per-device, add KV-layout assert, telemetry. will follow up in PR.

perf-bot: nightly alert resolved? once patch is up I'll re-run.

carmen: thanks all. ping me if you want the nvprof dump.
